q: Isotopes are the atoms of the same element with different ____.
e: Isotopes are the atoms of the same element with different masses. Masses is what this statement is using.

q: That is, they have the same number of protons but have different number of ____.
e: That is, they have the same number of protons but have different number of neutrons. Neutrons is what this statement is using.

q: In other words, isotopes have the same atomic number but have different ____ number.
e: In other words, isotopes have the same atomic number but have different mass number. Mass is what this statement is using.

q: Since isotopes of an element have same number of electrons, they have same electron configuration and thereby have the same ____ properties.
e: Since isotopes of an element have same number of electrons, they have same electron configuration and thereby have the same chemical properties. Chemical is what this statement is using.

q: They have different ____ properties as they vary in their atomic mass.
e: They have different physical properties as they vary in their atomic mass. Physical is what this statement is using.

q: Some isotopes are ____, that is, they do not decay (or transform) into other elements.
e: Some isotopes are stable, that is, they do not decay (or transform) into other elements. Stable is what this statement is using.

q: However, some are unstable (or ____), that is, decay into other elements.
e: However, some are unstable (or radioactive), that is, decay into other elements. Radioactive is what this statement is using.

q: Stable isotopes and some radioactive isotopes (____) exist naturally.
e: Stable isotopes and some radioactive isotopes (radioisotopes) exist naturally. Radioisotopes is what this statement is using.

q: Isotopes can also be produced artificially using nuclear reactors and particle ____.
e: Isotopes can also be produced artificially using nuclear reactors and particle accelerators. Accelerators is what this statement is using.

q: Every chemical element has one or more ____.
e: Every chemical element has one or more isotopes. Isotopes is what this statement is using.

q: For example, copper has two stable isotopes: ____ and $^{65}\text{Cu}$.
e: For example, copper has two stable isotopes: ^63Cu and ^65Cu. ^63cu is what this statement is using.

q: Three isotopes of hydrogen are: 1H (hydrogen), 2H(deuterium), and 3H(____).
e: Three isotopes of hydrogen are: 1H (hydrogen), 2H(deuterium), and 3H(tritium). Tritium is what this statement is using.

q: Tritium is ____. It transforms into helium isotope 3He.
e: Tritium is radioactive. It transforms into helium isotope 3He. Radioactive is what this statement is using.

q: Of over 1000 isotopes known thus far, the most abundant one in the entire universe is the hydrogen isotope ____.
e: Of over 1000 isotopes known thus far, the most abundant one in the entire universe is the hydrogen isotope ^1H. ^1h is what this statement is using.
